paragraphs: Approximate nearest neighbor search tries to find nearby data points without examining every possible match. Partition-based indexes make this manageable by dividing the search space. Existing supervised approaches learn partitions that place a training point together with its neighbors, making those neighbors accessible through lookup or backtracking.

This paper changes the learning target: it treats selecting candidate neighbors as a multilabel classification problem. Each possible neighbor corresponds to a label, and a query can have several correct labels. The partitions then act as classifiers for predicting which candidates should be considered. This connects the index structure directly to the candidate-selection task, rather than relying only on shared partition membership.

The empirical results suggest that the resulting classifier improves performance when paired with supervised or unsupervised partitioning strategies. The authors also establish a sufficient condition for a partitioning classifier to be consistent and verify it for chronological k-d trees. That condition provides a theoretical route to consistency; it does not establish that every partitioning strategy automatically satisfies it.
neurips-2022-a-multilabel-classification.tldr: Recasting candidate selection as multilabel classification improves partition-based neighbor search empirically and yields a sufficient condition for consistency.

paragraphs: Face recognition sometimes receives a collection of low-quality images rather than one clear photograph. Combining their features can improve recognition, but the combination must handle varying image quality and relationships among images. Attention mechanisms have quadratic complexity in the number of inputs, while recurrent approaches can make the result depend on input order.

Cluster and Aggregate divides feature fusion into two stages. First, it assigns the input features to a set of global cluster centers. Then, it combines the resulting cluster features. Aggregation therefore operates on the cluster summaries rather than directly on the entire collection. Those summaries also retain information from earlier images when new images arrive sequentially.

The update rule uses incremental averaging to achieve batch-order invariance. Consequently, processing images in differently ordered batches does not change their contributions, and earlier images do not lose influence simply because more time steps pass. Experiments on IJB-B and IJB-S support the effectiveness of this approach, combining scalability to large image sets with order-invariant sequential processing.
neurips-2022-cluster-and-aggregate-face-.tldr: Clustering image features before aggregation enables scalable face recognition with sequential updates that preserve batch-order invariance.

paragraphs: Periodic graphs contain local structures that repeat, as in crystal networks and polygon meshes. Generating them requires more than producing plausible connections: the output must preserve repetition while representing both local structure and global organization. The paper addresses these requirements with a generative model intended to learn such patterns automatically.

PGD-VAE separates its encoder into components for local and global patterns. Its decoder likewise divides the work among local structure, neighborhood, and global structure components. An assembler combines their outputs in a way that guarantees periodicity. This architecture gives the repeated building blocks and their larger arrangement distinct roles in the generation process.

The training objective additionally encourages graphs with the same local structure to receive invariant local representations. That supports the intended separation between what repeats locally and how the overall graph is organized. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The contribution is an architecture that incorporates periodic structure into both representation learning and output construction, addressing obstacles that general graph generation alone does not resolve.
neurips-2022-deep-generative-model-for-p.tldr: PGD-VAE separately learns local and global graph patterns and assembles generated structures with guaranteed periodicity.

paragraphs: Distributionally robust optimization seeks solutions that account for uncertainty about the data distribution. This paper studies the problem for convex losses and two specified forms of uncertainty: group-structured sets and sets bounded by an f-divergence. Its goal is to reduce the computational work needed to obtain an accurate solution.

The approach uses an accelerated optimization method built around a ball optimization oracle. This oracle is a subroutine that minimizes the objective within a small ball surrounding a supplied point. The main contribution is an efficient implementation of that local optimization subroutine for the distributionally robust objectives under consideration.

For N nonsmooth loss functions, the resulting algorithms reach epsilon accuracy using approximately N times epsilon to the power negative two-thirds, plus epsilon to the power negative two, first-order queries, with logarithmic factors suppressed. Relative to existing algorithms, the complexity improvement can be as large as a factor of epsilon to the power negative four-thirds. These are guarantees about query requirements for the specified convex problems, showing how efficient local optimization can support faster overall optimization.
neurips-2022-distributionally-robust-opt.tldr: Efficient local ball optimization enables accelerated algorithms with improved query complexity for specified convex distributionally robust problems.

paragraphs: Actor-critic reinforcement learning trains a policy to choose actions and a value function to estimate their longer-term consequences. These functions are commonly learned jointly. This paper finds that their learning tasks have noise levels differing by an order of magnitude, making joint learning suboptimal in the setting studied.

The authors instead learn the two tasks independently and connect them through a constrained distillation phase. They also find that the tasks benefit from different return estimates. Lower-variance estimates reduce policy-gradient noise, whereas lower-bias estimates reduce value-learning noise. These observations motivate allowing the policy and value function to use learning arrangements suited to their respective needs.

The resulting Dual Network Architecture, or DNA, extends Proximal Policy Optimization and significantly improves on its predecessor in the reported experiments. It also exceeds Rainbow DQN's performance in four of five tested environments, including more difficult stochastic control settings. The findings support separating the two learning problems while retaining a controlled way to transfer information between them.
neurips-2022-dna-proximal-policy-optimiz.tldr: DNA improves PPO by separating policy and value learning and accommodating their different noise characteristics.

paragraphs: This study investigates additional training aimed at reducing toxic language from pretrained language models. It examines three choices together: the adaptation corpus, the size of the model, and which parameters are updated. The models studied range from 126 million to 530 billion parameters, allowing the authors to examine detoxification across substantially different scales.

Using datasets generated by the models themselves consistently outperforms the existing baselines across model sizes in both automatic and human evaluations, including with a smaller training corpus. Model size alone does not remove the problem: models trained on the same pretraining corpus exhibit similar toxicity levels, while larger models require more effort to unlearn toxic content.

The paper also evaluates adaptation that adds and trains only adapter layers. For large models, this uses fewer trainable parameters and produces a better trade-off between toxicity and perplexity than adapting the whole model. Together, the findings show that corpus construction and adaptation strategy matter alongside scale, and that larger models are not automatically easier to detoxify.
neurips-2022-exploring-the-limits-of-dom.tldr: Self-generated adaptation data and adapter-only training improve detoxification, while larger models require more effort to unlearn toxic content.

paragraphs: Models handling real-time streams must cope with data whose distribution changes over time. This paper explores predictive modeling for unsupervised domain adaptation: using the stream's history to anticipate how a model should change before the next observation arrives. The intended benefit is lower adaptation latency.

The authors formulate this as continuous-time Bayesian filtering in a stochastic dynamical system. The evolving quantities are the adaptation model's parameters. Their extrapolative continuous-time Bayesian neural network, ECBNN, represents a distribution over those parameters together with its temporal dynamics. It can then project that distribution forward before observing incoming data, giving adaptation an anticipatory component.

The empirical results show improving parameter distributions generated from historical data alone during testing. The reported effects include low-latency adaptation without test-time training, progressively better alignment between source and target features, and improving performance over time. These findings support the proposed mechanism in the studied streaming setting; the improvement over time is an experimental finding rather than an unconditional guarantee for every changing stream.
neurips-2022-extrapolative-continuous-ti.tldr: ECBNN predicts how model-parameter distributions evolve, enabling low-latency adaptation without test-time training in the reported streaming experiments.

paragraphs: Training data can influence a classifier in ways that systematically disadvantage groups defined by sensitive attributes. This paper targets two particular fairness criteria, demographic parity and equality of opportunity. It asks whether a pretrained classifier can be improved by selectively reducing the influence of training examples associated with worse fairness.

The method uses an infinitesimal jackknife approach to estimate how individual training points affect the chosen fairness metric. Those estimates guide which examples to drop in principle. In practice, the corresponding intervention does not require fitting the model again, making the proposed change applicable to an already trained classifier.

Across experiments on diverse tasks, the intervention substantially improves the fairness metric without substantially reducing predictive performance, and consistently improves on the alternatives evaluated. The findings connect a model-level fairness problem to the influence of individual training examples. Because the selection is based on a particular metric, the reported improvement concerns that fairness objective rather than establishing an unrestricted guarantee of equitable behavior in every respect.
neurips-2022-fair-infinitesimal-jackknif.tldr: Fair Infinitesimal Jackknife improves selected fairness metrics by mitigating influential training points without refitting the classifier.

paragraphs: Stochastic gradient descent is used with complicated nonconvex objectives and noisy updates, but its theoretical guarantees often rely on more restrictive settings. The authors illustrate this mismatch using three canonical machine-learning models. They then develop results that accommodate much broader combinations of objective geometry and noise.

The first result establishes an either-or outcome: under nearly arbitrary nonconvexity and noise models, the sequence of SGD iterates globally converges to a stationary point or diverges. This characterizes possible long-run behavior without asserting that convergence always occurs. A stationary point is also not necessarily a globally optimal solution, so global convergence here should not be read as global optimality.

A second result imposes a somewhat stronger condition on how the objective and noise behave jointly. Under that condition, the objective function cannot diverge even if the parameter iterates do. This separates stability of objective values from stability of the parameters themselves. Together, the results extend the range of stochastic optimization problems for which SGD's long-run behavior can be characterized.
neurips-2022-global-convergence-and-stab.tldr: Broader SGD theory characterizes convergence or divergence and gives conditions keeping objective values stable even when iterates diverge.

paragraphs: SGD's success is often linked both to efficient optimization and to favorable generalization, but those explanations can be difficult to separate. This paper studies repeated passes of SGD over data in high-dimensional convex quadratic problems. That setting allows the authors to characterize learning behavior precisely rather than relying only on worst-case convergence rates.

They establish an asymptotic equivalence between SGD and a stochastic differential equation called homogenized SGD. Its behavior can be described explicitly through a Volterra integral equation. This yields formulas for how learning and risk evolve over time, allowing the optimization and generalization effects of stochastic updates to be examined separately.

The formulas reveal an implicit conditioning mechanism that explains SGD's efficiency relative to full-batch gradient descent. In the same setting, the authors prove that SGD noise harms generalization, ruling out implicit regularization there. They also extend the formalism to streaming SGD and predict the excess risk of repeated data passes relative to streaming. The conclusions about harmful noise are specific to the analyzed context.
neurips-2022-implicit-regularization-or-.tldr: For high-dimensional convex quadratics, exact risk analysis attributes SGD's efficiency to implicit conditioning while showing its noise harms generalization.

paragraphs: Prediction intervals are useful only if their reliability survives the conditions under which predictions are made. JAWS addresses uncertainty quantification under covariate shift, where the input distribution changes. Its core method, JAW, modifies jackknife+ using data-dependent likelihood-ratio weights to account for that shift.

The authors prove that JAW retains the same finite-sample coverage guarantee while relaxing jackknife+'s exchangeability assumption to accommodate covariate shift. They also introduce JAWA, computationally efficient approximations based on higher-order influence functions. Under common regularity assumptions, these approximations approach JAW's guarantee as sample size or influence-function order increases. The finite-sample result for JAW and the limiting result for JAWA are distinct guarantees.

The paper additionally reverses the usual interval-generation task: given a user-defined error tolerance, it estimates the probability that a prediction is erroneous. JAW-E and JAWA-E apply the proposed methods to this assessment. Experiments on biased real-world datasets show improvements over predictive-inference baselines for both interval generation and error assessment, connecting uncertainty guarantees to practical auditing questions.
neurips-2022-jaws-auditing-predictive-un.tldr: JAWS adapts jackknife-based uncertainty auditing to covariate shift, with coverage guarantees and methods for assessing prediction-error probabilities.

paragraphs: Moving an image should have a predictable effect on a vision model. For classification, the predicted category should remain unchanged; for segmentation, the pixel-level output should move with the image. These are shift invariance and shift equivariance, respectively. The paper addresses both through the layers that reduce and restore spatial resolution.

Learnable polyphase sampling, or LPS, provides paired downsampling and upsampling layers that can be trained end to end. The approach generalizes existing handcrafted downsampling layers and can be integrated into convolutional networks by replacing their sampling layers. This makes the sampling operation itself a learned part of obtaining consistent behavior under image shifts.

Experiments cover image classification and semantic segmentation. LPS matches or exceeds existing methods in both task performance and shift consistency. On PASCAL VOC segmentation, the authors report 100% shift consistency, an absolute improvement of 3.3% over the baselines, and describe this as the first achievement of true shift equivariance for that task. The result ties the architectural change to both prediction quality and predictable spatial behavior.
neurips-2022-learnable-polyphase-samplin.tldr: Learnable sampling layers enable shift-consistent convolutional networks, achieving 100% shift consistency in the reported PASCAL VOC segmentation evaluation.

paragraphs: This paper extends masked autoencoding to video by hiding randomly selected patches across space and time and training an autoencoder to reconstruct their pixels. The resulting task teaches representations from the video itself. Beyond patch and positional embeddings, the approach incorporates almost no explicit assumptions about spatial or temporal structure.

The experiments find that random masking without special treatment of space and time performs best. The optimal masking ratio reaches 90%, compared with 75% for images. This supports the hypothesis that useful masking levels relate to information redundancy. The high masking ratio also produces substantial computational savings, including reported wall-clock speedups greater than fourfold.

Using standard Vision Transformers, the method achieves competitive results on several challenging video datasets and can outperform supervised pretraining by large margins. Training on uncurated Instagram video data also gives encouraging results. Together, these observations suggest that masked reconstruction can support strong video representations with little domain-specific design, extending the case for masked autoencoding as a broadly applicable representation-learning framework.
neurips-2022-masked-autoencoders-as-spat.tldr: Reconstructing heavily masked video patches learns strong representations with minimal spacetime assumptions and substantial training speedups.

paragraphs: Incomplete datasets raise two related questions: how to fill in missing values, and which missing features would be most useful to acquire. This paper studies both for mixed-type data. It identifies restrictions in existing VAE approaches for this application: a single layer of latent variables and strictly Gaussian approximations to the posterior.

HH-VAEM replaces that setup with a hierarchical VAE and uses Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for improved approximate inference. Automatic tuning handles the sampling method's hyperparameters. The combination expands the latent structure used to model incomplete data and changes how the model approximates uncertainty about unobserved quantities.

Experiments show improvements over existing baselines in missing-value imputation and supervised learning with missing features. The paper also introduces a sampling-based method for efficiently estimating information gain when deciding which missing feature to acquire. That method outperforms alternatives based on Gaussian approximations in the experiments. The findings connect richer inference to both reconstructing absent information and selecting additional observations that are expected to be informative.
neurips-2022-missing-data-imputation-and.tldr: HH-VAEM combines hierarchical latent variables and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to improve missing-data inference and information-based feature acquisition.

paragraphs: Low-precision representations can reduce the energy and inference time of deployed neural networks. This paper asks how to allocate precision differently across individual weights and hidden activations while training the model. Its premise is that an efficient allocation need not give every parameter the same number of bits.

Directly optimizing discrete bit counts is intractable in the proposed framework. The authors approximate that problem by learning a noise magnitude for each parameter alongside its value. They extend the framework to activation precision as well, so weight values, weight precisions, and activation precisions can be learned together. The objective of efficient low-precision inference therefore influences the entire training process.

Experiments on convolutional networks trained on CIFAR and ImageNet produce highly varied precision assignments and improve on previous state-of-the-art quantization methods. The improvements also extend to reduced-precision GANs. These results support learning where precision matters within a network, using trainable noise as a practical route to an otherwise difficult discrete allocation problem.
neurips-2022-not-all-bits-have-equal-val.tldr: Training parameter-specific noise magnitudes enables joint learning of network values and heterogeneous numerical precisions.

paragraphs: State space layers can model long-range dependencies, but the effective S4 architecture requires a specialized matrix representation and computation. A simpler diagonal variant had shown that much of its performance could be retained with a particular initialization. This paper investigates why that simplification works and which design choices matter.

Although almost all state space models have an equivalent diagonal form, the authors show that initialization remains critical to performance. They establish that the diagonal approximation used by DSS recovers S4's dynamics in the limit of infinite state dimension. This supplies a mathematical explanation for the approximation without asserting that finite diagonal models exactly reproduce S4.

The authors then compare parameterization and computation choices in controlled experiments. Their resulting S4D model has a kernel computation expressible in three lines of code and performs comparably to S4 in almost all tested settings. It reports state-of-the-art results across image, audio, and medical time-series domains, alongside an 85% average on Long Range Arena. The findings show how careful initialization can make a much simpler architecture effective.
neurips-2022-on-the-parameterization-and.tldr: Carefully initialized diagonal state space models retain much of S4's performance while greatly simplifying kernel computation.

paragraphs: Large static datasets provide diverse examples, while interaction provides sequences shaped by an agent's actions. This paper combines those sources of learning by turning a pretrained generative model into an environment for exploration. The generator supplies images, and a new dynamical model determines how its latent input changes.

Each transition mixes an action with a randomly sampled latent and then uses an exponential moving average to provide temporal persistence. The pretrained generator decodes the resulting latent into an image. This creates an evolving visual environment from a model originally trained on static data, allowing exploration without requiring the original dataset itself to be interactive.

An unsupervised reinforcement learning algorithm explores the environment, and the collected observations support unsupervised representation learning. Their temporal relationships also provide a natural way to pair examples for supervision. Experiments suggest that the learned representations transfer successfully to downstream tasks in both vision and reinforcement learning. The contribution is a concrete mechanism for combining dataset diversity with action-dependent, temporally connected experience.
neurips-2022-palm-up-playing-in-the-late.tldr: Palm up turns a pretrained image generator into an explorable latent-space environment for learning transferable representations.

paragraphs: Image-text pairs collected online do not always correspond cleanly: a description may mismatch its image, while an unpaired description may still be compatible with it. PyramidCLIP addresses these problems by changing how visual and linguistic information are aligned during pretraining, rather than treating each pair as a perfect one-to-one match.

The method builds an input pyramid with multiple semantic levels for each modality. It aligns elements both at matching levels and through relationships across levels. It also softens the loss applied to unpaired examples, reducing pressure to force semantically compatible negative pairs apart. Both changes relax overly strict interpretations of the training pairs.

Experiments on five downstream tasks demonstrate the approach's effectiveness. With the same 15 million pretraining pairs, PyramidCLIP improves ImageNet zero-shot classification over CLIP for all three reported image encoders. At larger scale, its ResNet50 model trained on 143 million pairs surpasses CLIP trained on 400 million pairs on that task. These comparisons support the claim that hierarchical alignment and less rigid negatives improve data efficiency.
neurips-2022-pyramidclip-hierarchical-fe.tldr: PyramidCLIP improves vision-language learning through hierarchical alignment and softer negative-pair penalties, with reported gains in data efficiency.

paragraphs: Regret measures the accumulated shortfall from making less rewarding decisions while learning. This paper studies regret in episodic reinforcement learning with both model-free and model-based approaches. It considers general function and model classes, with results that depend on their eluder dimension, a measure of class complexity relevant to learning.

The key assumption is that every state has a gap between its best and second-best actions. Exploiting this instance-specific separation, the authors show regret that grows logarithmically with the time horizon T. This differs from guarantees that must hold uniformly without using the particular problem's action gaps.

The paper further shows that logarithmic regret can be achieved with only O(log T) policy switches. Thus, strong cumulative performance does not require continually replacing the policy throughout execution. Matching lower bounds establish that logarithmic dependence cannot generally be improved even in tabular problems. The results connect efficient learning with infrequent adaptation, while keeping the action-gap assumption central to the claimed regret rate.
neurips-2022-reinforcement-learning-with.tldr: With a best-action gap at every state, episodic RL can achieve logarithmic regret with only logarithmically many policy switches.

paragraphs: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning can become harder as more agents participate. This paper studies a setting with permutation-invariant agents, where reordering the agents should not change the underlying problem. It examines how transformers can represent relationships among those agents and how that structure affects theoretical learning guarantees.

The authors establish transformers' ability to implement complex relational reasoning and develop both model-free and model-based offline learning algorithms using transformer approximators. Their analysis gives suboptimality bounds with different dependence on agent count: independent of that count for the model-free algorithm and logarithmic in it for the model-based algorithm. These bounds mitigate the growth in difficulty associated with many agents.

The results rely on a new transformer generalization bound and an analysis of maximum-likelihood estimation of system dynamics. The authors identify their model-based method as the first provably efficient MARL algorithm to explicitly exploit agent permutation invariance. The generalization bound may also apply to other transformer regression problems, extending the potential relevance of the analysis beyond multi-agent learning.
neurips-2022-relational-reasoning-via-se.tldr: Transformer-based offline MARL algorithms exploit permutation invariance to obtain suboptimality bounds with mild dependence on agent count.

paragraphs: Score-based generative models rely on approximations to intermediate distribution scores and the final distribution of their forward process. This paper investigates what those approximations mean for the generated samples. Its focus is whether samples lie on the underlying data manifold, the potentially low-dimensional set containing the relevant kinds of data.

The authors establish precise conditions under which a model produces samples from that manifold. Their example is a manifold of face images: meeting the conditions ensures that generated outputs are faces. It does not necessarily ensure that different faces appear with the correct relative frequencies. Producing the right kind of object and reproducing its full probability distribution are therefore separate achievements.

The same analysis also helps characterize memorization. If the manifold is taken to be the set of training examples, the results specify when generation memorizes those examples. This provides a first step toward understanding generalization, linking approximation behavior to both manifold recovery and the possibility of reproducing only the observed training data.
neurips-2022-score-based-generative-mode.tldr: The paper gives conditions for score-based models to generate samples on a data manifold and characterizes when they memorize training examples.

paragraphs: Sparse PCA seeks principal components that involve relatively few input dimensions, making them easier to interpret than components spread across all dimensions. Finding these sparse components is a separate algorithmic challenge, especially in high dimensions. This paper studies how far the powerful Sum-of-Squares family of algorithms can go in solving it.

The authors establish lower bounds linking sample count, sparsity, and ambient dimension. In the identified regimes, Sum-of-Squares methods fail to recover the component optimally even when given sub-exponential running time. This constrains the possibility that their strength on other statistical problems will translate into better sparse PCA recovery than simpler established methods.

Combined with known algorithms, the results give an almost complete picture of efficient sparse PCA behavior and strengthen the case for the optimality of existing approaches. Their reach matters because Sum-of-Squares encompasses many techniques, including spectral and statistical-query approaches. The authors also extend their lower-bound techniques to Tensor PCA, obtaining analogous trade-offs for this higher-order variant.
neurips-2022-sub-exponential-time-sum-of.tldr: Lower bounds show that even sub-exponential-time Sum-of-Squares algorithms cannot optimally solve sparse PCA in specified sample, sparsity, and dimension regimes.

paragraphs: Automatically optimizing tensor programs requires both a useful set of possible implementations and an effective way to search that set. This paper focuses on a practical bottleneck: existing search spaces can be difficult for domain experts to extend. New optimization knowledge is less useful if incorporating it requires substantial changes to the system.

MetaSchedule introduces a domain-specific probabilistic programming abstraction for describing the search space. Experts can inspect a program and express stochastic choices that compose program transformations in a modular way. A learning-driven framework then searches the resulting space for an optimized program. This separates describing available transformations from finding a useful combination of them.

Experiments show that the abstraction can modularly cover search spaces used by state-of-the-art tensor optimization frameworks. It also lets experts expand those spaces and improve the system through additional modules. The reported extensions produce a 48% speedup on end-to-end deep-learning workloads. The contribution combines an extensible language for optimization choices with a framework that learns how to search them.
neurips-2022-tensor-program-optimization.tldr: MetaSchedule makes tensor-program search spaces modular and extensible, with learning-driven optimization yielding a reported 48% workload speedup.

paragraphs: Backdoor training examples can affect an entire neural network, making their influence difficult to remove afterward. Trap and Replace changes the training arrangement so that the harmful behavior is encouraged to concentrate in a small classification head. That head can then be replaced while retaining the shared feature extractor.

During the first stage, an auxiliary image-reconstruction head shares the network stem with a lightweight classification head. Reconstruction encourages the stem to preserve useful low-level visual information rather than overfit to misleading backdoor correlations. The less-protected classifier becomes the easier place to learn those correlations, leaving the stem largely unpoisoned according to the proposed mechanism.

During the second stage, the stem is fixed and a fresh classification head is trained using a small clean holdout dataset. This clean data is part of the defense's procedure. Evaluations against ten backdoor attacks show improvements over previous state-of-the-art defenses in attack success rate and clean classification accuracy across CIFAR10, GTSRB, and ImageNet-12. The strategy makes removal easier by shaping where harmful behavior is learned.
neurips-2022-trap-and-replace-defending-.tldr: Trap and Replace directs backdoor learning toward a small classifier, then replaces it using clean holdout data.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization chooses new observations by optimizing an acquisition criterion. That creates an optimization problem inside the larger search. The acquisition function can have many local optima, lack differentiability, or otherwise frustrate numerical optimizers. A common response is to evaluate it on a discrete collection of randomly chosen candidate points.

This paper proposes constructing candidates from a Delaunay triangulation of the inputs already evaluated. These triangulation candidates, called tricands, use the geometry of the existing input design to determine the discrete search set. The change concerns where the acquisition criterion is evaluated, providing an alternative to both continuous numerical optimization and random candidate generation.

The authors describe the construction and evaluate it on synthetic benchmarks and real simulation experiments. Tricands outperform both numerically optimized acquisition approaches and random-candidate alternatives in those evaluations, and they also work well in hybrid schemes. The results show that the candidate set itself can materially influence Bayesian optimization performance, with existing observations supplying useful structure for the inner search.
neurips-2022-triangulation-candidates-fo.tldr: Candidates derived from a Delaunay triangulation improve Bayesian optimization over random candidates and numerical acquisition optimization in reported experiments.
